key_insight: Locating the bow shock with inviscid tracking and treating it as a viscous-domain boundary enables high-order hypersonic simulations without resolving the shock structure.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports prediction of hypersonic surface pressure and heating while avoiding extreme shock-layer mesh compression and coupled viscous shock-tracking optimization.
method: Apply high-order implicit shock tracking (HOIST) to the Euler equations on a coarse mesh to locate and align the bow shock.
Discard upstream elements and remesh the post-shock domain to resolve the boundary layer.
Solve compressible Navier–Stokes equations with high-order interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin, prescribing shock-boundary states using oblique shock relations.
evidence_signal: Tests on a Mach 10.6 axisymmetric blunt cone, Mach 17.6 cylinder, and Mach 5 three-dimensional sphere showed surface pressure and heat flux in good agreement with experiments and reference computations.
watch_item: Using an inviscidly determined shock as a fixed viscous-domain boundary warrants validation where viscous effects substantially alter shock position or geometry.
paper_title: A shock-fitting approach to high-order simulation of viscous hypersonic flows based on inviscid implicit shock tracking
